data.name: Qatada
data.gender_notes: Qatada is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'qatadah' which means 'young man' or 'follower'. In Islamic tradition, Qatada refers to a scholar or a student of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The name Qatada carries the meaning “Young man, follower” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Qatada usually hope their child will grow to embody young man, follower and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Qatada is a name that represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, with a deep understanding and connection to the spiritual and religious teachings of Islam.
data.etymology: Qatada belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young man, follower.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qatada total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: قطادة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي يعني القوي الشديد
in_arabic.long_meaning: قطادة هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، ويعني القوي الشديد، وقد ورد ذكره في بعض المصادر العربية القديمة، وهو من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني القوة والشدة، وقد يكون له علاقة بالقطيدة وهو الشيء الذي يقطع أو يشد

in_urdu.name: قطادہ
in_urdu.meaning: قوی اور مضبوط شخص کے لئے استعمال ہونے والا مذکر نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: قطادہ ایک عربی मूल کا مذکر نام ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے قوی اور مضبوط۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم کے قبل از اسلام استعمال ہوتا تھا، اور آج بھی مسلم کمیونٹیز میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ اس نام کا ذکر بعض قدیم عربی مصادر میں ملتا ہے، اور یہ قوت اور مضبوطی کے معنی رکھتا ہے

in_hindi.name: क़तादा
in_hindi.meaning: एक मजबूत और शक्तिशाली व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाने वाला नाम
in_hindi.long_meaning: क़तादा एक अरबी मूल का नाम है, जिसका अर्थ है मजबूत और शक्तिशाली। यह नाम इस्लामी पंचांग से पहले से उपयोग किया जाता था, और आज भी मुस्लिम समुदायों में उपयोग किया जाता है। इस नाम का उल्लेख कुछ प्राचीन अरबी स्रोतों में मिलता है, और यह शक्ति और मजबूती के अर्थ रखता है

in_pashto.name: قطاده
in_pashto.meaning: د قوي او مضبوط سړي لپاره کارول شوی نوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: قطاده د عربي اصلي نوم دی، چې د قوي او مضبوط معنی لري. دا نوم د اسلامي تقويم نه مخکې کارول شوی و، او نن هم د مسلمانانو په ټولنو کې کارول شوی دی. دغه نوم د ځينو پخوانيو عربي سرچينو کې يادونه شوی دی، او د قوت او مضبوطۍ معنا لري

data.cultural_impact: The name Qatada holds significant cultural value in the Islamic community, highlighting the importance of education and the pursuit of knowledge. Qatada signifies a young man who is diligent, committed, and focused on learning and preserving the wisdom and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). This cultural significance emphasizes the role of scholars in preserving and transmitting the Islamic faith, its teachings, and its traditions to future generations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Qatada also carries a deep spiritual meaning in Islamic tradition. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is believed to be the Last Prophet of God, and the Quran is considered the final revelation of God to mankind. Qatada, as a student or follower of the Prophet, embodies the quest for spiritual enlightenment and the pursuit of a deeper understanding of God and His teachings. In this way, the name Qatada represents a commitment to seeking and spreading knowledge, knowledge that can lead to personal and collective spiritual growth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Qatada ibn Di'amah al-Qurashi was a prominent scholar of the early Islamic period. He was born in Medina and studied under Anas ibn Malik and Ibn Abbas. He was known for his rigorous approach to Hadith and his opposition to the Mu'tazili school of thought.

modern_usage.modern_context: Qatada ibn Di'amah is a significant figure in Islamic history, particularly in the field of Hadith scholarship. His rigorous approach to the study and transmission of Hadith has influenced scholars for centuries.
